newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end lower.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end lower.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended lower in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Monday.
"The interbank rate rose slightly today but activity was quiet. Treasury bill yields were slightly higher bond prices were lower. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.30/2.25 percent compared with Friday's yield of 2.17/2.12 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.85/1.80 percent against 1.68/1.63 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$99.00/99.05 from Friday's close of S$99.23/99.28, September 2001 at S$99.08/99.13 versus S$99.23/99.28 and June 2003 at S$99.53/99.58 against S$98.83/98.88.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 3-1/8 3- percent from Friday's 3-1/4 3-1/8 percent.
